claims.location: source name SILAC light rows 228 rows, 1-6 ... 445-450
claims.evidence: Label key sheet "SILAC" lists 37 Sample IDs, each with its raw file pattern (e.g. AML1001_Blasts_BM -> AML1001_Blast_BM_2D_Fxx.raw). The 38th deposited group, AML1036_Blast_BLD_2D_F01-F06, is absent from that sheet; its ID AML1036_Blasts_BLD is taken from the file name and the NPM1 sheet (Gr07 channel 2). Suffix _SILAC distinguishes these sample preparations from the same patients' TMT samples.

claims.location: comment[label] rows 228 rows, 1-6 ... 445-450 and 228 rows, 7-12 ... 451-456
claims.value: SILAC light = patient blasts; SILAC heavy = spike-in standard
claims.evidence: MaxQuant summary_new.txt: Multiplicity 2, Labels0 empty, Labels1 Arg10;Lys8 on all 228 searched runs (rule 14 verified: really multiplexed SILAC). The patient material is cryopreserved primary cells sorted by FACS and lysed directly (PRIDE sampleProcessingProtocol; Supplemental Methods "Nucleic acid and protein extraction") - no culture step, so it cannot carry a metabolic label: patient = light. Data check (proteinGroups_new.txt): HBB (haemoglobin from blood/marrow specimens) Intensity L >> H in all 38 experiments (e.g. AML1024 L 5.9e10 vs H 1.5e8), and MPO L > H in most - the light channel holds the clinical specimen, the heavy channel cultured (labelled) cells; total L and H intensities are ~1:1 (H/L 0.57-1.14), consistent with a 1:1 spike-in.

claims.location: source name / characteristics[sample type] / characteristics[phenotype] SILAC heavy rows 228 rows, 7-12 ... 451-456
claims.value: SILAC heavy reference standard (spiked into <Sample ID>) / reference / "SILAC heavy (Arg10/Lys8) labelled spike-in reference standard, composition not reported"
claims.evidence: Rule 18: the heavy channel of a spiked-in labelled standard is encoded as reference, not as a study sample. Its composition (which cell line(s)) is not stated in the paper, PRIDE, the label key or the search output, so organism part, cell type, pooled sample, disease, material type, age, sex and individual are not available and no cell line is named. One heavy source per patient mix keeps the (source, replicate, fraction, label) coordinate unique (precedent PXD030422).

claims.location: characteristics[organism] rows 1-456
claims.evidence: PRIDE organisms NEWT:9606. Heavy rows: the search used a human-only FASTA (uniprot_taxonomy_9606_Reviewed.fasta) and heavy intensities pair 1:1 with light across thousands of human protein groups, so the standard is human material.

claims.location: characteristics[organism part] SILAC light rows
claims.value: bone marrow / blood (from label key Source BM / PB / Apheresis); not available for AML1027
claims.evidence: SILAC sheet column "Source": BM -> bone marrow; PB and Apheresis (leukapheresis product = peripheral blood) -> blood. AML1027 (rows 433-438): Sample ID AML1027_Blasts_BLD and file name "BLD" contradict Source "BM" (also BM in the FH UW45 sheet) -> not available. AML1036 (rows 445-450): no Source column; "BLD" in file name and NPM1-sheet ID -> blood.

claims.location: characteristics[cell type] SILAC light rows
claims.evidence: The samples are FACS-sorted viable leukemic blasts (uVLBs) (PRIDE protocol; paper). CL:0001064 malignant cell; same choice as campaign precedent PXD030422.

claims.location: characteristics[phenotype] + characteristics[genotype] + factor value[genotype] SILAC light rows
claims.value: blast immunophenotype from label key "Blast IP"; "FLT3-ITD <Pos/Neg/ND>; NPM1 mutation <Pos/Neg>" from label key
claims.evidence: SILAC sheet columns Blast IP (VLBCD34+ / VLBCD117+ / VLBCD45/SSC; legend in Table S13 and Fig. 2: CD117+ = CD34-negative, CD45/SSC = double negative) and FLT3-ITD / NPM1. AML1036 has no SILAC-sheet row: phenotype not available (the sorted fraction can differ between arms for the same patient, e.g. AML044 VLBCD45/SSC in SWOG27 vs VLBCD34+ in NPM1 Gr05), genotype from the NPM1 sheet (FLT3 Pos, NPM1 Pos; mutation status is patient-level and agreed across sheets for every overlapping patient checked). Genotype is the compared variable: the study compares FLT3-ITD and NPM1 mutant vs non-mutant blasts (paper Results; Table S15).

claims.location: characteristics[disease] SILAC light rows
claims.evidence: All patients are de novo AML (PRIDE protocol; paper). MONDO:0018874 verified in OLS. Heavy rows: not available (standard of unreported origin).

claims.evidence: No digestion protocol is published for the SILAC arm. MaxQuant summary_new.txt Enzyme = Trypsin, Enzyme mode = Specific; PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol "tryptic enzyme constraint". A specific-trypsin search identifying >6000 protein groups is consistent with a tryptic digest; the column permits only not applicable as a reserved word.

claims.evidence: Filled by sdrf-tools build from ms-proteomics.

claims.location: comment[data file] / comment[technical replicate] / assay name all rows
claims.evidence: Each of the 228 deposited SILAC .raw files appears twice (light + heavy row); file names exactly as in PRIDE files/all; one injection per mix, so technical replicate 1.

limitations: techsdrf is not installed; instrument, activation, collision energy and MS2 detector were read from HTTP-range raw headers of one file per run group (9 files), not from every file.

Precursor mass tolerance for the three MaxQuant searches is not recorded in the deposited parameters.txt/summary.txt; 20 ppm is the value the PRIDE dataProcessingProtocol and Supplemental Methods state ("Peptide MH+ mass tolerances were set at 20 ppm"). MaxQuant's main-search default is 4.5 ppm (first search 20 ppm), so the stated value may describe the first search.
Ancestry is not reported for any individual: characteristics[ancestry category] = not available on all rows.

Individual-level age, sex, treatment response and clinical data exist only for the 30 Table S13 patients (SWOG27 + FHCC/UW-HDR3). They were propagated by patient ID to the same patients' samples in other arms (AML1050, AML039, AML044, AML058, AML158, AML179, AML185 in the NPM1 arm); all other patients carry not available. Sex/channel concordance was checked with RPS4Y1 reporter intensity: 27/27 SWOG27 channels and 7/7 NPM1-arm overlap channels agree with Table S13 (AML179: Table S13 sex F but karyotype 46,XY[20]; RPS4Y1 is low in both of its channels, so sex female was kept).

No patient age, sex or individual-level clinical data were deposited for the SILAC-arm, NPM1-arm or E3 patients other than the S13 overlaps; the NPM1 label key gives only Age_Group (Adult/Ped), used for developmental stage (adult) and clinical data (pediatric).
SCOPE NOTE: this file covers the 228 SILAC runs (38 patients x 6 fractions x 2 channels). The 408 TMT runs are in PXD029216-tmt.sdrf.tsv (rule 12).

The composition of the heavy (Arg10/Lys8) SILAC standard is not reported anywhere (paper, supplement, PRIDE, label key, MaxQuant output); heavy rows are encoded as a reference of unknown composition. The SILAC arm itself is not described in the publication.

AML1036_Blast_BLD_2D_F01-F06 and AML1027_Blast_BLD_2D_R2_F01-F06 (24 rows) are not covered by the deposited MaxQuant search (which instead names undeposited AML1027 (non-R2) and AML1089 runs). Their tolerances are not applicable (rule 5); their modification parameters repeat the arm's SILAC chemistry. Because convert-openms cannot parse "not applicable" tolerances, `parse_sdrf convert-openms` fails on the full SILAC file and succeeds on the 432 searched rows; see validation.txt.
Raw headers show original acquisition names (e.g. JK033016_AML_RO10001_2D_F01.raw for AML1036, RO50479 for AML1027_R2): the deposited files were renamed; the name->patient mapping is the submitter's.
AML1027 organism part: Sample ID/file name say BLD, label-key Source says BM -> not available.
